title: Normalized coefficient projection interfaces
statement: Let C and X be sites with object and morphism universes c and v, essentially small in the coefficient universe r. For sheaves of commutative rings R use the actual module-sheaf category Mod(J,R) and its ordinary unbounded derived category D(J,R) [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Scalars is a family of actual ordinary scalar-extension functors and universal K-flat left derived presentations [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Geometry consists of the ring and module algebraic lifts of a geometric inverse image, its exact additive module functors and normalized module adjunctions with K-injective direct images [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Comparisons records ordinary inverse-image/scalar isomorphisms normalized by insertion, and their derived isomorphisms normalized by the computation maps on flat-term K-flat complexes. ScalarUnits records the ordinary multiplication isomorphism and its derived representative. Define comparison as the mate of the inverse-image comparison under the coefficient geometric adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Define targetAssociator by balanced scalar associativity including the image of ring composition, and successive as the normalized two-step mate word. Laws is the conjunction of the projection cocycle, multiplication-unit and commuting-square equations; ShiftLaws records counit-normalized scalar shifts and compatibility of comparisons, mates, associators and unitors. Assertion(J,K) universally quantifies the geometric and scalar presentations and asserts existence of these normalized comparison/unit data satisfying Laws and ShiftLaws. These are the unchanged interfaces of the parent cocycle statement, relocated to an independent module so its geometric lemmas can import them without a cycle.
